related_questions.question: How to recover quickly from COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: To recover quickly from COVID-19, focus on rest, hydration, and symptom management. Getting plenty of sleep, staying hydrated, and taking over-the-counter medications for fever or body aches can help accelerate recovery. If you're vaccinated, you may experience less severe symptoms and recover faster according to WebMD.
snippet_highlighted_words: focus on rest, hydration, and symptom management

list.title: Rest:
list.snippet: Prioritize sleep and avoid strenuous activities. Aim for more than the recommended 7-9 hours of sleep for adults.

list.title: Hydration:
list.snippet: Drink plenty of fluids to stay hydrated, especially if you have a fever.

list.title: Symptom Relief:
list.snippet: Over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen or ibuprofen can help manage fever and body aches.

list.title: Hygiene:
list.snippet: Practice good hygiene by washing your hands frequently and avoiding close contact with others.

list.title: Monitor Your Health:
list.snippet: Pay attention to your symptoms and seek medical advice if they worsen or if you experience any emergency symptoms.

related_questions.question: What is the best way to get rid of COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: The best way to get rid of COVID-19 involves a combination of self-care at home, preventative measures, and, in some cases, medical treatment. Staying home and apart from others, particularly while experiencing symptoms, is crucial to prevent further spread. This includes wearing a mask when around others, practicing good hygiene like handwashing, and disinfecting frequently touched surfaces. For those at higher risk of severe illness, medications may be available to help treat COVID-19, according to the CDC.
snippet_highlighted_words: a combination of self-care at home, preventative measures, and, in some cases, medical treatment

list.snippet: Stay home: If you have symptoms or test positive, isolate yourself from others in your household.
Mask up: Wear a face mask when around others, even if you're feeling better, to minimize potential spread.
Hygiene: Wash your hands frequently with soap and water for at least 20 seconds.
Cover coughs and sneezes: Use a tissue or your elbow to cover your mouth and nose.
Clean and disinfect: Regularly clean and disinfect surfaces that are frequently touched.
Ventilation: Improve airflow in your living space to help reduce the concentration of virus particles, according to the Mayo Clinic.
Separate living spaces: If possible, use separate bathrooms and bedrooms.

list.title: Consult with a healthcare professional:
list.snippet: If you are at higher risk for severe illness, talk to your doctor about available treatment options.

list.title: Medications:
list.snippet: In some cases, medications like antivirals may be prescribed to help reduce the severity of illness.

list.title: Fever-free:
list.snippet: You can return to being around others after you haven't had a fever for 24 hours without using fever-reducing medication.

list.title: Symptom improvement:
list.snippet: Even after returning to normal activities, it's still a good idea to continue practicing preventative measures like wearing a mask and maintaining good hygiene, especially for the five days following isolation from the Mayo Clinic.
